```{shinylive-r}
#| standalone: true

# This is a Shiny web application. You can run the application by clicking
# the 'Run App' button above.
#
# Find out more about building applications with Shiny here:
#
#    https://shiny.posit.co/
#

library(shiny)

# Define UI for application that computes Riemann sums
ui <- fluidPage(
  
  # Application title
  titlePanel("Discrete-Time Dynamical Systems"),
  
  # Sidebar with a slider input for number of bins 
  sidebarLayout(
    sidebarPanel(
      selectInput("model", "Select updating function", c(Logistic = "logistic", Custom = "user")),
      conditionalPanel(
        condition = "input.model == 'logistic'",
        sliderInput("r",
        withMathJax(
        helpText("\\(r\\) (parameter)")),
                    min = 0,
                    max = 4,
                    value = 2,
                    step = 0.01),
        sliderInput("x0",
                  withMathJax(
        helpText("\\(x_{0}\\) (initial value)")),
                  min = 0,
                  max = 1,
                  value = 0.5,
                  step = 0.01),
      ),
      conditionalPanel(
        condition = "input.model == 'user'",
        textInput("expr", label = "f(x) = ", value = "0.5*x + 1", placeholder = "e.g., 5*x+7"),
        sliderInput("xmax",
                    "Graph window",
                    min = 1,
                    max = 50,
                    value = 5),
        sliderInput("x0",
                  withMathJax(
        helpText("\\(x_{0}\\) (initial value)")),                  min = 0,
                  max = 50,
                  value = 0.5,
                  step = 0.1),
      ),
      sliderInput("n",
                  "Number of steps",
                  min = 10,
                  max = 50,
                  value = 10,
                  step = 5)
    ),# ends sidebarPanel
    
    # Show a plot of the generated distribution
    mainPanel(
      withMathJax(
        helpText("Choose values for the window size, initial value, and number of steps.  This app will generate a cobwebbing diagram for \\[x_{n+1} = f(x_{n}).\\] You can choose 'Logistic' to study  \\(x_{n+1} = rx_{n}(1-x_{n})\\) and experiment with the value of \\(r\\) which stretch the graph vertically. Or, you can choose 'Custom' and enter your own function and choose its graphing window. When you enter the formula, use * for multiplication. The graph will update, but you must enter something for the formula, preferably involving the variable \\(x\\).")
      ),
      plotOutput("cobweb")
    )# end mainPanel
  )# ends sidebarLayout
)# ends fluidPage

# Define server logic required to graph a function and rectangles for area approximation
server <- function(input, output) {
  
  output$cobweb <- renderPlot({
    # generate bins based on input$bins from ui.R
    if(input$model == "logistic"){
      r <- input$r
      xmax <- 1
      f <- function(x) r*x*(1 - x)
    }else{
      xmax <- input$xmax
      if(grepl("x", parse(text = req(input$expr)), ignore.case = TRUE) & length(input$expr)>0){
        f <- function(x)eval(parse(text = tolower(req(input$expr))))
      }else if(length(input$expr)>0){
        f <- function(x) eval(parse(text = req(input$expr))) + 0*x
      }
    }
    
    # this will let us use the sliders by their assigned variable name rather than require "input$" each time
    
    x0 <- input$x0
    n <- input$n
    
    par(mar = c(4.1, 4.1, 1.8, 0.8), mfrow = c(1, 2), xaxs = "i", yaxs = "i")
    plot(f, xlim = c(0, xmax), ylim = c(0, xmax), las = 1, lwd = 2, xlab = "", ylab = "")
    mtext(expression(x[n]), 1, line = 2, font = 2, cex = 1.35)
    mtext(expression(x[n+1]), 2, line = 2, font = 2, cex = 1.35)
    mtext("Cobwebbing diagram", 3, pos = 0.5, font = 2, cex = 1.35)

    abline(a = 0, b = 1, lty = 3, col = "gray")
    points(x0, 0, pch = 19, col = "red")        
    xs <- x0
    
    # step over each subinterval
    for(i in 2:n){
      x0 <- f(x0)
      xs <- c(xs, x0)
      if(i == 2){
        segments(xs[i-1], 0, xs[i-1], xs[i])
        segments(xs[i-1], xs[i], xs[i], xs[i])}
      else{
        segments(xs[i-1], xs[i-1], xs[i-1], xs[i])
        segments(xs[i-1], xs[i], xs[i], xs[i])
      }
    }
    
    plot(seq(along = xs)-1, xs, type = 'o', pch = 19, xlab = "", ylab = "", ylim = c(0, xmax), las = 1)
    points(0, xs[1], col = "red", pch = 19)
    mtext(paste(expression(n), "(step number)"), 1, line = 2, font = 2, cex = 1.35)
    mtext(expression(x[n]), 2, line = 2, font = 2, cex = 1.35)
    mtext("Solution", 3, pos = 0.5, font = 2, cex = 1.35)
    # to add our answer, we plotted a point to orient outselves around the graph
    # points(b, 0.3)
    # more clever would be to calculate the max value of f(x) on the interval and use that rather than 0.45, 0.4
    # I changed those a bit after class
    # then if we allowed sliders for additional parameters in the function, the graph and text would update
  })
}

# Run the application 
shinyApp(ui = ui, server = server)
```
